# Fablenest Publishers

> Fablenest Publishers is a children’s book publishing service. We help authors turn a manuscript or an idea into a finished, professionally made book, with editing, illustration, cover design, formatting, a book trailer, an author website and marketing support.

## Services

### Book Publishing
Our book publishing service takes your manuscript through editing, cover design, interior formatting and publication, so you end up with a professionally made book that is ready to reach readers in print and as an ebook.

- Q: What is included in your book publishing service?
  A: Manuscript preparation (editing and proofreading), book cover design, interior formatting, and support with submitting your book to the publishing platform you choose.

- Q: I have never published a book. Can you guide me?
  A: Yes. We explain each stage in plain language, so you can make informed decisions without needing any publishing experience.

- Q: Do you help with the book cover?
  A: Yes. Cover design is part of the service. We create a cover that reflects your book and works well as a small thumbnail online.

- Q: Which platforms can my book be published on?
  A: We can prepare your book for the major platforms, including Amazon Kindle, Barnes & Noble, IngramSpark and Lulu, depending on your goals.

- Q: Can I publish a book that is already written but not edited?
  A: Yes. Manuscript preparation covers editing, proofreading and content refinement, so your text is polished before it is formatted.

Book publishing is the work between a finished manuscript and a book a reader can buy: editing, cover design, interior layout, file preparation and setting up the book on selling platforms.

Steps:
1. Review the manuscript: We read your text and agree what editing and proofreading it needs.
2. Edit and proofread: The text is edited for clarity and checked for spelling, grammar and consistency.
3. Design the cover: A cover is designed that reflects the story and is easy to read at thumbnail size.
4. Format the interior: Text and pictures are laid out for print and for ebook readers.
5. Publish: The finished files are uploaded to the platform you chose and the book page is set up.

### Book Illustrations
Our book illustration service creates the characters, page illustrations and cover artwork for your children’s book. You approve the style and the sketches, then receive finished, full-colour artwork prepared for print and ebook.

- Q: What does a children’s book illustration service include?
  A: Character design, illustrations for each page or spread, cover artwork, rounds of revisions, and final files prepared for print and ebook.

- Q: Can I choose the illustration style?
  A: Yes. We show you styles that suit your story, such as watercolour or bold digital colour, and you approve one before the full artwork begins.

- Q: How many illustrations does a picture book need?
  A: It depends on the length and format of your book. We review your manuscript and recommend how many spreads or pages to illustrate.

- Q: Will I see sketches before the final artwork?
  A: Yes. You review rough sketches first and can request changes before they become finished illustrations.

Illustrating a children’s book means designing the characters and drawing the scenes that tell the story alongside the words. It is done in stages so you can guide the look before the artwork is finished.

Steps:
1. Your hand-drawn idea: You can sketch the idea on paper, as rough as you like. It only shows us what you imagine.
2. Line art: Our artist redraws the idea with clean lines, and you can ask for changes before colour is added.
3. Colour: After the lines are approved the artist adds colour, mood and light.
4. Final illustration: Details, shading and background finish the picture, ready for print and screen.

### Author Branding
Author branding gives you a consistent look, voice and story across your books, website and social media. We help you define your author story and visual identity, and deliver a simple brand kit you can reuse everywhere.

- Q: What is author branding?
  A: It is the look, voice and story that make you recognisable as an author, such as your colours, fonts, logo, bio and the way you talk to readers.

- Q: Why does a children’s author need a brand?
  A: Parents, teachers and librarians choose books from authors they recognise and trust. A consistent brand across your books and pages makes you easier to remember.

- Q: What do I get at the end?
  A: A brand kit with your author story, logo or mark, colour palette, fonts and bios, ready to use on your website, covers and social media.

- Q: Can the brand match my existing books?
  A: Yes. We can build on the style of your current books so everything feels like it belongs together.

Author branding is the look, voice and story that readers connect with your name. It covers things like your bio, colours, fonts and logo, and it makes your books, website and social media feel like they belong together.

Steps:
1. Discover: We learn about you, your books and the readers you want to reach.
2. Explore directions: We show two or three directions for colours, fonts and tone.
3. Refine: We polish the direction you choose.
4. Deliver a brand kit: You receive final files and a simple guide you can reuse.

### Author Website
An author website is your own home on the internet, where readers can learn about you, find your books and buy them. We design and build a mobile-friendly site with a page for each book, a newsletter sign-up and a contact form.

- Q: Do I need an author website?
  A: It is not required, but it is the one place online that you fully control. It helps readers, parents and schools find your books, and gives you somewhere to send people from social media.

- Q: What pages will my website have?
  A: Usually a home page, an about page, a page for each book with buy links, a news or blog page, and a contact page with a newsletter sign-up.

- Q: Will it work on phones?
  A: Yes. Most visitors use a phone, so every page is designed to work well on small screens first.

- Q: Can I update the website myself?
  A: Yes. We set it up so you can add a new book or a news post without needing a developer, and we show you how.

An author website is a site you own where readers can learn about you, see your books and find where to buy them. Unlike social media, you control it, and it stays useful for years.

Steps:
1. Plan the pages: We agree the pages, features and the content you will provide.
2. Design: You review the layout on desktop and on a phone.
3. Build: We build the site and add your books and text.
4. Launch: We test everything, publish the site and show you how to update it.

### Social Media Marketing
Our social media marketing service helps your children’s book reach parents, teachers and readers. We set up your profiles, plan and schedule content, run a launch campaign, and report on what is working each month.

- Q: Which social platforms do you work with?
  A: We choose platforms based on where your readers are, which for children’s books often means Instagram and Facebook, and sometimes others. We recommend the best fit during the audit.

- Q: Who do children’s books need to reach on social media?
  A: Mostly the adults who buy and recommend them: parents, grandparents, teachers and librarians. Content is planned with them in mind.

- Q: Will I approve posts before they go out?
  A: Yes. You see the content plan and posts first, so nothing is published without your approval.

- Q: How do I know whether it is working?
  A: You receive a plain-language monthly report that shows what was posted, how people responded and what we will adjust next.

Social media marketing means sharing your book and your story on platforms where parents, teachers and readers already spend time, in a regular and planned way.

Steps:
1. Audit: We look at your current pages and your audience.
2. Plan: We choose platforms and themes that suit your book and write a content calendar.
3. Create and schedule: Posts are made, approved by you and scheduled.
4. Review: We report what worked and adjust the plan.

### Book Trailer
A book trailer is a short film, usually 30 to 60 seconds, that gives readers a quick taste of your story. We write the script, plan the storyboard, animate your artwork with music, and deliver versions for web and social media.

- Q: What is a book trailer?
  A: A short promotional film for a book, similar to a movie trailer. It shows the mood and the best moments of the story without giving away the ending.

- Q: How long is a book trailer?
  A: Most are between 30 and 60 seconds, which is long enough to build interest and short enough for people to watch to the end.

- Q: Where can I use my trailer?
  A: On your website and book page, on social media, in emails to schools and libraries, and on video platforms.

- Q: Do I need illustrations to make a trailer?
  A: Illustrations make a trailer much stronger. If you already have them we animate them. If you do not, our illustration service can create them first.

A book trailer is a short video, usually 30 to 60 seconds, that shows the mood and best moments of a book without giving away the ending. It is used to make people curious about the story.

Steps:
1. Brief: You tell us the tone, the length and where the trailer will be shown.
2. Script and storyboard: We write a short script and plan each shot for you to approve.
3. Produce: Your artwork is animated and combined with music and, if you want, a voice.
4. Deliver: You receive versions sized for your website and for social media.

### Press Release
A press release is a short, formal announcement of your book sent to journalists, bloggers and librarians. We write it in the correct format, build a media list suited to children’s books, and send it at the right moment.

- Q: What is a press release for a book?
  A: A news announcement about your book, written in a standard format so editors, bloggers and librarians can quickly see what the book is and why it matters.

- Q: When should I send a press release?
  A: Usually around your launch date, so coverage can appear when readers can actually buy the book. We help you choose the timing.

- Q: Who receives the press release?
  A: We build a list of outlets and contacts that cover children’s books, such as parenting sites, local media and library or school newsletters.

- Q: Does a press release guarantee coverage?
  A: No. It gives your news the best chance of being noticed and picked up, but editors decide what they publish.

A press release is a short, formal announcement of news. For a book it tells journalists, bloggers and librarians that the book exists, what it is about and why it is worth mentioning.

Steps:
1. Share the facts: You give us the book details, the launch date and a quote.
2. Find the angle: We choose what is most newsworthy and write the headline.
3. Build a media list: We choose outlets that cover children’s books.
4. Send and follow up: The release goes out at the right time and we follow up where it makes sense.

### Copyright Registration
Copyright registration creates an official record that you are the author of your book. We guide you through the process: checking which registration applies, preparing the application, filing it and passing you the registration record. This is not legal advice.

- Q: Is my book protected by copyright without registering?
  A: In many countries copyright exists automatically when you create the work. Registration adds an official public record, which can be useful if you ever need to prove or enforce your rights.

- Q: What do I need to register a book?
  A: The title, your name as author, details of publication and a copy of the work. We tell you exactly what is needed for your situation.

- Q: Is this legal advice?
  A: No. We help with the administrative process only. For legal questions about your rights, please speak with a qualified lawyer.

- Q: Which country’s office do you register with?
  A: It depends on where you live and where you publish. We confirm the right office with you before filing.

Copyright registration is an official record that you are the author of a book. In many countries copyright exists automatically, but registering gives you a public record that can help if someone copies your work. This page is information, not legal advice.

Steps:
1. Check eligibility: We confirm which registration applies to your book and country.
2. Collect the details: You confirm the title, author name and publication details.
3. File: We complete and submit the application, including the filing fee.
4. Receive the record: The registration confirmation is sent to you and kept with your files.
